9. The Question on the Factors of Sakka “Venerable Nāgasena, when you say that ‘three factors of Sakka are to be adopted,’ which are those three factors to be adopted?
“Just as, Great King, Sakka is endowed with absolute happiness;”
In the same way, Great King, a yogi practicing yoga should be devoted to the bliss of absolute seclusion.
This, Great King, is the first quality of Sakka that should be adopted.
Furthermore, Great King, when Sakka sees the gods, he exerts himself and gives rise to joy.
In the same way, Great King, the yogin practicing yoga must uplift his mind toward wholesome states—unshrinking, untiring, calm—and he must generate joy, exert himself, strive, and endeavor.
This, Great King, is the second quality of Sakka that should be adopted.
Furthermore, Great King, dissatisfaction does not arise in Sakka.
In the same way, Great King, a yogi practicing yoga should not give rise to dissatisfaction while in an empty dwelling.
This, Great King, is the third quality to be adopted from Sakka.
And this was said, Great King, by the Elder Subhūti:
“O Great Hero, since I went forth into your teaching,
I do not recall anything arisen [that would cause me to fall].”
“The mind is connected with sensual desire.
Thus ends the ninth question of Sakka’s limbs.
